title: Join translations give a natural simplicial homotopy resolution
statement:
Use simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and standard simplices, spaces and coherent colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and weak homotopy equivalences and Kan replacement of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Write $\langle X\rangle$ for the space represented by a Kan replacement of a simplicial set $X$. For each small simplicial set $X$ and integer $n\geq0$, define a simplicial set $t_nX$ by
$$(t_nX)_m=X_{n+m+1}.$$
For a monotone map $\beta:[m']\to[m]$, its operator is restriction along the ordinal-sum map $\mathrm{id}_{[n]}\star\beta:[n]\star[m']\to[n]\star[m]$, where $[n]\star[m]=[n+m+1]$, with the first block preceding the second. Restriction along $\alpha\star\mathrm{id}_{[m]}$ for $\alpha:[n']\to[n]$ makes $n\mapsto t_nX$ a simplicial diagram. Restriction to the first block gives a map $p_n:t_nX\to\operatorname{disc}(X_n)$, where $\operatorname{disc}(T)$ has the same set $T$ in every degree and identity operators. Restriction to the last block gives an augmentation $e_n:t_nX\to X$, compatible with the diagram in $n$.

For every $n$, $p_n$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The coherent cocone induced by $e_\bullet$ exhibits $\langle X\rangle$ as the colimit of $n\mapsto\langle t_nX\rangle$ in spaces. These assertions and the displayed maps are natural in $X$ and in the indicated simplex operators; no Kan condition on $X$ is required.

source.place: Notation 1.3.4.11 and Lemmas 1.3.4.12-1.3.4.13, printed pp.112-113 Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopical result.

proof.text: Put $B_{n,m}=X_{n+m+1}$. For monotone maps $\alpha:[n']\to[n]$ and $\beta:[m']\to[m]$, the two restriction operators commute, since $(\alpha\star1)(1\star\beta)=\alpha\star\beta=(1\star\beta)(\alpha\star1)$ on the ordered blocks. Composition and identity operators follow from the same equality. This defines the bisimplicial set $B$ and the diagram $n\mapsto t_nX$. The first-block inclusion commutes with every last-block operator; hence its restriction is the simplicial map $p_n$ to the constant set $X_n$. The last-block inclusion commutes with every first-block operator; hence its restriction is an augmented simplicial diagram $e_\bullet$. For $f:X\to Y$, the equality $fX(\gamma)=Y(\gamma)f$ for every ordinal map $\gamma$ proves naturality of both maps and of all displayed operators.

source.place: Notation 1.3.4.11; verification of both ordinal-sum variables and augmentations.

proof.text: Fix $n$. The faces and degeneracies of $t_nX$ in degree $m$ are $D_i=d_{n+1+i}$ and $S_i=s_{n+1+i}$, respectively. For the augmentation $p_n$ define $h_{-1}:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ and $h_m:X_{n+m+1}\to X_{n+m+2}$ by the same formula $s_n$: duplicate the last vertex of the first block, placing its copy at the start of the second block. Then $p_{n,0}h_{-1}=1$, $D_0h_m=d_{n+1}s_n=1$, and $D_1h_0=d_{n+2}s_n=s_nd_{n+1}=h_{-1}p_{n,0}$. For $0\leq i\leq m+1$, $D_{i+1}h_{m+1}=d_{n+2+i}s_n=s_nd_{n+1+i}=h_mD_i$; for $0\leq i\leq m$, $S_{i+1}h_m=s_{n+2+i}s_n=s_ns_{n+1+i}=h_{m+1}S_i$. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction] holds, including the augmented degree $-1$, and it gives a simplicial section and a simplicial homotopy of its composite with $p_n$ to the identity.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.12; explicit contraction replacing the omitted contractibility assertion.

proof.text: A simplicial homotopy $A\times\Delta^1\to A$ realizes to a continuous homotopy: by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], $|A\times\Delta^1|=|A|\times_k[0,1]$, and composing the realized map with this identification gives the homotopy with the prescribed endpoints. Apply this to the section and homotopy in Step 2. On realizations $p_n$ is a homotopy equivalence. It induces a bijection on components; at a basepoint its two induced homomorphisms are inverse up to the basepoint-change isomorphism along the homotopy path. Therefore every based homotopy-group map is an isomorphism, exactly the weak-equivalence definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This proves the first clause for arbitrary $X$, without requiring any horn fillers.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.12; passage from the explicit simplicial contraction to weak equivalence.

proof.text:
Fix $m$ and instead vary $n$. The augmented simplicial set $H_n=B_{n,m}$ has faces $d_i$ and degeneracies $s_i$ in the first block, and augmentation to the constant set $X_m$ by deleting that block. Reverse this simplicial direction: set $V_n=H_n$, with $d_i^V=d_{n-i}$ and $s_i^V=s_{n-i}$ in degree $n$. These are simplicial operators, since conjugating an ordinal map $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$ to $i\mapsto b-\alpha(a-i)$ preserves its order and composition. Set $h_{-1}=s_0:X_m\to X_{m+1}$ and $h_n=s_{n+1}:X_{n+m+1}\to X_{n+m+2}$. Its extra-degeneracy equations are $\varepsilon h_{-1}=1$, $d_0^Vh_n=d_{n+1}s_{n+1}=1$, $d_1^Vh_0=d_0s_1=s_0d_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon_0$, and
$$d_{i+1}^Vh_{n+1}=d_{n+1-i}s_{n+2}=s_{n+1}d_{n+1-i}=h_nd_i^V,$$
$$s_{i+1}^Vh_n=s_{n-i}s_{n+1}=s_{n+2}s_{n-i}=h_{n+1}s_i^V.$$
The ranges are respectively $0\leq i\leq n+1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. Apply [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction] and Step 3's realized-homotopy argument. The reversal does not change the realized homotopy type: the formula $[z;(u_0,\ldots,u_n)]\mapsto[z;(u_n,\ldots,u_0)]$ gives an involutive homeomorphism $|V|\to|H|$, since conjugation of every ordinal operator reverses the same coordinates in the quotient relation. It commutes with augmentation to $X_m$. Thus $H\to\operatorname{disc}(X_m)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. These contractions need not commute with the other variable; the augmentation itself does, by Step 1.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.13; agent proof by contracting the other direction, with the reversal and all extra-degeneracy equations explicit.

proof.text:
Let $E_{n,m}=X_m$, constant in $n$. The maps $B_{n,m}\to E_{n,m}$ of Step 1 form a map of bisimplicial sets and, for each fixed $m$, Step 4 proves a weak equivalence in the $n$ direction. Apply the exchanged-direction clause of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence]. Its diagonal is the weak equivalence
$$a:\operatorname{diag}B\longrightarrow X,\qquad a_r:X_{2r+1}\to X_r$$
given by restriction to the last $r+1$ vertices. We next verify the coherent colimit property, rather than equating a weak-equivalence assertion with that property.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.13; diagonal weak equivalence of the augmentation.

proof.text: Work with the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and its Reedy diagram model structure on $\mathsf{sSet}^{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}$ from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Every such bisimplicial object is Reedy cofibrant. Indeed, in each fixed inner degree its latching colimit consists of the outer degenerate simplices: the unique surjection/nondegenerate factorization of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] identifies two presentations exactly through their common nondegenerate presentation. Thus the latching map is degreewise injective, including degree zero where its source is empty. Cofibrations in the Kan model structure are precisely these monomorphisms, so in particular $B$ is Reedy cofibrant. All index categories here are the small ordinary category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the same universe.

source.place: Examples A.2.9.8 and A.2.9.21; direct latching verification.

proof.text: For a bisimplicial set $Z$, let $LZ=\int^{[n]}Z_n\times\Delta^n$. In degree $r$ its elements are classes $(z,\alpha)$, $z\in Z_{n,r}$, $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$, with relation $(Z(\gamma)z,\alpha)\sim(z,\gamma\alpha)$. The map $(z,\alpha)\mapsto Z(\alpha)z\in Z_{r,r}$ is well-defined, with inverse $z\mapsto(z,1_{[r]})$; the relation shows both composites are identities. The inner operator and the outer operator commute, so this is a simplicial identification $LZ=\operatorname{diag}Z$. Giving a map from this coend to $K$ is, by the same relation and cartesian currying, giving a natural family $Z_n\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,K)$. Hence $L$ is left adjoint to $R(K)_n=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,K)$. These are explicit set-valued coends and adjunctions, with no homotopy-colimit assertion assumed.

source.place: Example A.2.9.29; explicit coend, inverse and adjunction.

proof.text:
The adjunction in Step 7 is Quillen. For a Kan fibration $u:K\to K'$, the relative matching map of $R(u)$ in outer degree $n$ is
$$\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,K)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^n,K)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^n,K')}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,K').$$
This follows by restricting a map to all proper faces, whose union is the boundary (also $n=0$, with empty boundary). Lifting a horn against this map is, by cartesian currying, lifting $u$ against the pushout product of $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with that horn. The boundary is mono and the horn is anodyne by the trivial-cofibration characterization of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; their pushout product is anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. Thus the matching map is a Kan fibration. If $u$ is trivial, lift boundaries instead of horns: the pushout product of two monomorphisms is a monomorphism, since degreewise its domain is the union of two subsets of the product. A trivial Kan fibration lifts against every monomorphism, by the cited model structure and its weak factorization system. The matching map is therefore a trivial fibration. The relative matching characterization of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] proves that $R$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. By adjunction of lifting squares, preservation of these two right classes says that $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, exactly the left-side hypothesis of the derived-adjunction theorem. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to obtain the coherent derived adjunction.

source.place: Examples A.2.9.29-31; direct relative matching proof of the coend Quillen adjunction.

proof.text:
We now construct the comparison with spaces by enriched functors. Let $\mathcal S_*,\mathcal K_*,H_0,H_{\mathcal S},H_{\mathcal K}$ and $a,b,j,h,i,v$ be exactly those of [lem-coef-kan-enriched-hammock-comparison]. The three specified functors $a,b,j$ are Dwyer--Kan equivalences. Apply the functorial locally Kan replacement $R$ and coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] to the entire zigzag, including its commutative square $ahi=jbv$. This gives equivalences
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R\mathcal K_*)\xrightarrow{\simeq}N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RH_{\mathcal K})\xrightarrow{\simeq}N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RH_{\mathcal S})\xleftarrow{\simeq}N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RH_0).$$
The category $\mathcal K_*$ is locally Kan: [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] states that $\operatorname{Fun}(A,K)$ is Kan whenever $K$ is Kan, for every $A$. Thus its replacement map induces an equivalence $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal K_*)\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R\mathcal K_*)$. Put $\mathcal S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal K_*)$, the coherent category of spaces and their simplicial mapping objects in the statement. By [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization], $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RH_0)$ together with $N(h)$ and replacement is the universal localization $\mathcal S_0[W^{-1}]_\infty$, compatible with actual maps. Inverting the first two displayed equivalences and the replacement equivalence constructs a functor equivalence $E:\mathcal S_0[W^{-1}]_\infty\to\mathcal S$. The equality $ahi=jbv$ makes $Eqi$ coherently equivalent to $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(v)$, where $q$ is localization; hence this comparison is already compatible with the actual functor on all ordinary Kan complexes, not just its objectwise mapping spaces.

For all simplicial sets, choose a functorial fibrant replacement $\eta:1\to T$ by factoring the terminal maps in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; $TX$ is Kan and $\eta_X$ is a trivial cofibration. Applying $Eq$ to $\eta$ gives a coherent transformation from $Eq$ to $EqiT$, and every component is an equivalence because $q$ inverts $W$. The componentwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes it a natural equivalence. Combining it with $Eqi\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(v)$ gives $Eq\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(v)T$ as functors on the entire ordinary category of simplicial sets. This identifies $qX$, its maps, every diagram and its transformations with $\langle X\rangle$ and their specified Kan-replacement images. The derived adjunction of Step 8 can therefore be transported through this actual functor equivalence and the corresponding functor-category equivalence. Composition coherence comes from the cited simplicial functors and their commutative square; no composition compatibility is inferred from separate frame mapping spaces.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433, with Section 7.4, p.437; independent enriched-hammock route to spaces. Universal-localization and derived coherent-nerve inputs are separately cited nodes; functor compatibility from the strict square and the natural fibrant-replacement transformation.

proof.text:
For Kan $K$, the natural maps $K\to R(K)_n$ are constant maps on $\Delta^n$. Each is a simplicial homotopy equivalence by [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance], applied to $\Delta^n\to\Delta^0$: its realization is the collapse of a convex simplex and is a weak equivalence, with no nonemptiness assumption on $K$. These maps commute with every ordinal operator. Since $R$ is right Quillen, $R(K)$ is Reedy fibrant; its derived image is consequently represented by this diagram. The constant-diagram comparison and restriction compatibility in [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification] identify it with the coherent constant diagram on $\langle K\rangle$. Step 6 says $B$ is already cofibrant. The derived adjunction of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] therefore gives, naturally in every space $\langle K\rangle$,
$$\operatorname{Map}(\langle\operatorname{diag}B\rangle,\langle K\rangle)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\langle B_\bullet\rangle,\operatorname{const}\langle K\rangle).$$
By the dual mapping-space criterion for cocones in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], this is the full universal property of a colimiting cocone: its corepresented map is an equivalence for every target. Its cocone is furnished by the coend maps $B_n\times\Delta^n\to\operatorname{diag}B$: these are the ordinary adjunction unit, followed by the inverse of the constant-diagram equivalence, and the derived-adjunction theorem identifies the unit coherently. Finally compose with the weak equivalence $a$ of Step 5. The composite $B_n\times\Delta^n\to\operatorname{diag}B\xrightarrow a X$ is exactly $e_n$ after projection to $B_n$. Indeed in degree $r$, a pair $z\in X_{n+r+1}$, $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$ first restricts along $\alpha\star1_{[r]}$, then along the last block; the composite is the original last-block inclusion, independent of $\alpha$. Hence the resulting coherent cocone is the specified $e_\bullet$, and is colimiting with apex $\langle X\rangle$. All coend formulas, adjunction units and the last-block equality commute with maps of $X$; thus this is the asserted natural cocone, not merely an equivalence of possible apex objects.

source.place: Corollary A.2.9.30 and Example A.2.9.31; mapping-space and actual augmentation verification for HA Lemma 1.3.4.13.
